justification: Fixes a real, live, recurring production crash: Railway's dcp-extract cron OOM-killed (exit -9) three separate nights (2026-09-08/09) while opening a 139MB canterbury_bankstown PDF with pdfplumber, and because there was no size check before that call, the OS kill took the WHOLE process down mid-batch -- every other queued chapter (46 of 47 that night) silently never got extracted, not just the oversized one. Not Critical: no schema/query change, purely an early-return guard using a value already computed one line above. Not Minor: this was actively breaking a real production pipeline nightly.

pre_impl.existing_data: url_content_length / downloaded pdf_path.stat().st_size -- both already computed, no new query. Reuses the exact 30MB threshold already documented and used advisorily by scripts/dq_probe_oversized_pdf_oom_risk.py (DQ-98, registered 2026-09-07).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: N/A -- pure control-flow addition, no data assumption changed.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future dcp-extract run, any council, any chapter over 30MB -- not council-specific. Currently affects 7 active chapters (per dq_probe_oversized_pdf_oom_risk.py at registration time; canterbury_bankstown carries the bulk: 13 chapters, 326MB combined, one single chapter at 139MB).

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The guard stops firing (an oversized PDF reaches DCPExtractor/preflight_layout again), it false-positives on a normal-sized PDF (blocks legitimate small chapters), the skip-status DB write/alert stops firing or dedup breaks (re-alerts on an unchanged file, or never alerts at all), or dry_run stops being a real no-DB-writes guarantee.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: BEFORE this fix: no test existed for this path at all -- the only evidence of the bug is the real Railway crash log (exit -9, 2026-09-06/08/09) and the DQ-98 tracker entry. AFTER fix: 8 tests -- (1) dry_run=True: an over-threshold PDF is skipped, returns (False, None), and NEVER touches conn.cursor() or DCPExtractor/preflight_layout (monkeypatched sentinels that raise if called, not a plain Mock().assert_not_called()); (2) not dry_run, active chapter never-alerted-before: sends exactly one Telegram alert naming the council/chapter and writes the oversized_pdf status key + conn.commit(); (3) not dry_run, SAME content_hash+size already recorded: sends ZERO alerts (dedup) but still refreshes the status row's timestamp; (4) not dry_run, chapter no longer active (Sol MEDIUM 0.94): fetchone() returns no row under the is_active=TRUE filter -- sends ZERO alerts, issues ZERO update, and rolls back; (5) the SELECT itself carries both FOR UPDATE and is_active=TRUE, asserted directly against the executed SQL text (Sol MEDIUM 0.98) -- not just the resulting behavior, so a future edit that drops the row lock while keeping the same behavior in the mocked tests would still be caught; (6) an under-threshold PDF (real file at exactly threshold-1 bytes, not a 4KB stand-in -- Sol LOW 0.99 on an earlier version) proceeds to DCPExtractor exactly as before; (7) a PDF at EXACTLY the threshold also proceeds (boundary is strict >); (8) the constant literally equals 30*1024*1024, guarding against silent drift from the probe script's own literal. All 8 pass. Fixing test (4) also surfaced a latent bug in test (2): its original mock used fetchone()->None to mean 'never alerted', which is actually the SAME return shape as 'no row found' -- the correct mock for 'row exists, column is NULL' is fetchone()->(None,), a 1-tuple. Corrected. The UPDATE-call-counting filter in tests (2)/(3)/(4) also had to change from a naive 'UPDATE' in sql substring match to sql.strip().upper().startswith('UPDATE ') once the SELECT itself started containing the substring 'FOR UPDATE'.

functions.name: extract_chapter
functions.file_line: scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py:2904 (function def; size guard + skip-status write added inside the existing early-return block starting ~2934, OVERSIZED_PDF_SKIP_BYTES constant at module scope just above the def)
functions.input: Same as before -- chapter dict, s3 client, conn, dry_run, review. New: reads pdf_path.stat().st_size (already computed for the existing log line) once more for the comparison; on the oversized+not-dry_run path only, also reads chapter['content_hash'] and chapter['id'] (both already present on every chapter dict from _pending_chapters_sql -- no new query).
functions.output: Unchanged return shape: tuple[bool, dict|None]. New early-exit path returns (False, None) -- identical shape to the pre-existing R2-download-failure early exit 3 lines above it. Side effect added (Sol HIGH 0.96, not dry_run only): SELECT ... WHERE id=chapter_id AND is_active=TRUE FOR UPDATE (Sol MEDIUM 0.94 added is_active, Sol MEDIUM 0.98 added FOR UPDATE row-locking so no concurrent transaction can flip is_active while the alert decision is in flight), a best-effort Telegram send via run_monitors.send_telegram deduped against the row's existing last_suspect_alert_key, then UPDATE ... SET last_suspect_alert_key/_at WHERE id=chapter_id AND is_active=TRUE + conn.commit() (which releases the row lock); the whole block is skipped and conn.rollback() called if the SELECT finds no active row, or if any step raises.
functions.if_none: N/A -- no new None-producing input; the guard is a size comparison on a value that always exists once the download succeeds. content_hash defaults to the literal string 'nohash' in the alert key if the registry row genuinely has none, rather than erroring.

break_it.scenario: [Sol HIGH 0.96, RESOLVED same PR] A skipped chapter left no DB-visible trace -- only a Railway log line -- so stale regulatory content kept being served with zero signal that a real source update was ever seen and dropped (e.g. a genuinely valid 31MB replacement PDF with real amended controls would be silently skipped forever).
break_it.what_happens: A reviewer or operator checking why a chapter hasn't updated would find nothing in the database pointing at the real cause.
break_it.how: extract_chapter() now writes a distinct oversized_pdf status to dcp_chapter_registry.last_suspect_alert_key/_at (reusing the existing suspect-alert columns/convention, a separate reason namespace so it can never collide with an extraction-produced suspect_reason) and sends one Telegram alert per distinct (content_hash, size) -- deduped so an unchanged oversized file doesn't spam the channel every night, but a genuinely new oversized replacement does alert. Full UI-level staleness surfacing (a badge in the review/public UI) is still NOT built -- that's a separate, larger feature, not folded into this stability patch.

break_it.scenario: [Sol HIGH 0.91, ACKNOWLEDGED not fixed -- was already this report's break_it #2] Compressed PDF byte size does not bound pdfplumber's DECODED memory use -- a file under 30MB with pathological compression, large content streams, or many page objects could still pass the guard and OOM-kill the whole batch.
break_it.what_happens: A pathological small-but-complex PDF still crashes the whole batch exactly as before this PR, just less often (only chapters the byte-size proxy happens to miss).
break_it.how: Not fixed here -- confirmed as a real, structural limit of a byte-size-only guard, same caveat the existing probe script already documents (page count / layout complexity / embedded raster images likely matter as much as raw bytes). Sol's suggested real fix -- per-chapter subprocess isolation with an enforced memory limit, OR the chunking approach -- IS the actual DQ-98 fix, and the user already explicitly chose to register DQ-98 and build its real fix as separate follow-up work rather than design it now. Folding subprocess isolation into what was meant to be a narrow stability patch would re-open that already-made scope decision unilaterally. Recorded in .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md's DQ-98 entry (2026-09-09 update) so the fix direction reflects this refinement.
break_it.repro: N/A -- inherent to a byte-size heuristic; no code change to demonstrate. See DQ-98 tracker entry.

break_it.scenario: [Sol LOW 0.99, RESOLVED same PR] The original under-threshold test only wrote a 4KB file, not a real file near the 30MB boundary -- a future threshold change (e.g. quietly narrowed to 20MB) would not have been caught by that test.
break_it.what_happens: The boundary itself could silently drift without any test failing.
break_it.how: Rewrote to write a REAL file of exactly threshold-1 bytes via seek+write (sparse, fast, but a genuine file of that size on disk), and added a same-shape exact-threshold test (size == OVERSIZED_PDF_SKIP_BYTES must still proceed, since the guard is strictly-greater-than).

break_it.scenario: [Sol MEDIUM 0.94, RESOLVED same PR] The skip-status SELECT and UPDATE (added the previous push, for the HIGH 0.96 finding above) omitted is_active = TRUE -- a chapter deactivated between batch selection and this code running would still get alerted about and have its registry row mutated as though still served, this project's own pre-pr-review rule #1 (every SELECT needs correct WHERE-clause scope).
break_it.what_happens: A pointless stale-content alert for a chapter no longer served, and a status write on a row nobody should be tracking any more.
break_it.how: Both the SELECT and UPDATE now carry AND is_active = TRUE. If the SELECT returns no row (deactivated, or genuinely gone), the alert AND the write are both skipped entirely -- not just the alert.

break_it.scenario: [Sol MEDIUM 0.98, RESOLVED same PR] The is_active fix above still had a time-of-check/time-of-use gap: deactivation landing BETWEEN the SELECT and the Telegram send (not between the SELECT and the UPDATE) would still fire the alert -- already decided at read time -- even though the later UPDATE would then correctly match zero rows and skip the write. Net effect: exactly the spurious inactive-chapter alert the is_active fix claimed to prevent, just via a narrower window.
break_it.what_happens: One spurious Telegram alert for a chapter that became inactive in the split second between the read and the network call.
break_it.how: The SELECT now takes FOR UPDATE, row-locking that one chapter from the read through conn.commit() -- a concurrent is_active=FALSE write on the SAME row blocks until this transaction ends, so no other transaction can flip it while the alert decision is in flight. A single atomic UPDATE...RETURNING (write-then-alert-if-affected) was considered and rejected: it would mark the row alerted before the Telegram call actually succeeds, silently swallowing a failed send instead of retrying it next run -- the exact failure mode the pre-existing suspect-alert block's own comment warns against. Kept send-then-write, just made the read atomic against concurrent deactivation via the row lock.

break_it.scenario: This is a STABILITY guard, not the DQ-98 fix -- chapters over 30MB (7 active right now, canterbury_bankstown's the majority) will now be skipped, loudly, forever, until chunked extraction is actually built. They will never complete extraction under this fix alone.
break_it.what_happens: Those specific chapters' regulatory content can never be refreshed via the automated pipeline -- same limitation DQ-98 already documents (P2, 'those specific chapters can never be kept current via the automated pipeline until this is fixed'), unchanged by this PR.
break_it.how: Deliberately out of scope -- DQ-98's full fix (chunked extraction via pypdf/pikepdf page-range slicing, with the named clause-boundary risk) was explicitly registered as separate follow-up work by the user's own prior decision, not re-litigated here. This PR only stops the crash from taking down the OTHER 40 chapters in the same nightly batch.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_oversized_pdf_oom_risk.py -- still reports the same active oversized chapters after this PR merges; that count is expected to stay non-zero until DQ-98 itself ships.

break_it.scenario: The guard fires AFTER the full R2 download completes (pdf_path.stat().st_size needs the file on disk), not before -- a 139MB download still happens over the network every night before being discarded.
break_it.what_happens: Wasted bandwidth/R2 egress on every retry of an oversized chapter, though this is a small cost next to the crash it prevents and the existing code already downloads before any size decision was possible.
break_it.how: Not addressed here -- R2's HEAD-based url_content_length (already in dcp_chapter_registry, already used by dq_probe_oversized_pdf_oom_risk.py) could in principle gate BEFORE download in a future iteration, but that couples extract_chapter to registry-freshness assumptions this fix doesn't need to make; the guard against the actual crash (pdfplumber.open on a huge in-memory file) is what matters and is fixed regardless.
break_it.repro: N/A -- efficiency note, not a correctness defect.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- confirm the next scheduled dcp-extract run (03:00 UTC nightly) completes for the 40 non-oversized chapters instead of crashing the whole batch; Railway alert should show '[SKIP] ... 30MB' lines for the oversized ones instead of exit -9.
